blocks.text: Using SCIM operations enables you to perform operations such as creating and deleting users and groups. To do this, you must enable SCIM-based provisioning and have your Base URL and Bearer Token. Most API calls to Zscaler SCIM servers require the Bearer Token for authentication. However, there are several API calls (e.g., /Schemas, /ServiceProviderConfig, and /ResourceTypes) that do not require authentication, as they are informational for the SCIM server and not particular to any organization.
Zscaler SCIM servers have the following rate limits:
To avoid retries, configure your application to comply with these rate limits.
For a full list of operations supported by the Zscaler SCIM servers, as well as attribute mappings, see Understanding SCIM.

blocks.heading: Updating a User's Display Name, Email, and Department

blocks.text: To update user information, use the following operations:
In this example, the PUT request is used.
curl -X PUT -v -k <Base URL>/Users/{UserID} -d @updated_user_file_example.json -H "Authorization: Bearer <Bearer Token>"-H "Content-Type: application/scim+json"

blocks.heading: Updating a Group With a New Member

blocks.text: To update a group, use the following operations:
In this example, the PUT request is used.
curl -v -k -X PATCH <Base URL>/Groups/{GroupID} -d @patch_scim_group_1.txt -H "Authorization: Bearer <Bearer Token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json-patch+json"
The server responds with 204 - No Content upon successful operation.
